title: Jewish student at Syracuse University reacts to fraternity hate crime - NewsBreak
text:
By Allie Elkins No media credit provided. ,
1 hours ago
SYRACUSE, N.Y. (WSYR-TV) — A Syracuse University student believes the school needs to do something after two students were charged with hate crimes after their antisemitic actions at a fraternity .
“You have to take this stuff seriously,” Elliot Pototsky said. “It all builds up and eventually becomes worse and worse.”
Pototsky wasn’t involved in the incident, but he is part of the Jewish community on campus.
The incident involved a student accused of crashing a fraternity’s Rosh Hashanah dinner and throwing pork on the walls and floor.
The other student is accused of driving the first student to and from the fraternity house, before being caught by police, according to the DA and Syracuse University administrators.
Potonsky arrived on campus less than three months ago to begin grad school at the S.I. Newhouse School of Public Communications
“It’s definitely startling,” Pototsky said. “I haven’t been in the Syracuse community that long.”
While we don’t have confirmation on what motivated this attack, Potonsky suggested common sense comes first.
“If it sounds like something that’s a stupid thing to do in our current moment of society, we probably shouldn’t be doing it,” he said.
He still celebrated Rosh Hashanah on campus and received a warm welcome from a Rabbi on campus.
“We just had a very nice exchange,” Pototsky said. “He told me to come by any time for Friday night services.”
In a statement , Syracuse University called the incident “abhorrent, shocking to the conscience, and violates our core value of being a place that is truly welcoming to all. It will not be tolerated at Syracuse University.”
